start.text: (An old man with a steel tumbler, behind the counter.) Come in, come in — under the shutter. Rameshwara Tiffin Room. Forty-one years. No idli today. Coffee, if the generator holds.

diesel.text: Three nights. Maybe four, if nobody wants coffee.

radio.text: Raju from the Whitefield darshini rang the landline before it died. Shut in his own kitchen. Two of them at his counter. (He looks at you.) Someone young should go.

bye.text: Tomorrow, at first light. Noise helps — they go to noise.

again.text: The generator. The shelf. Coffee at six.

dark.text: (The generator is cold.) That was the last of the diesel. The army has lamps at Cubbon — the bandstand, they say. We go while we can still walk to it.

go.text: Forty-one years. (He pulls the shutter down behind him, and locks it anyway.)

camp.text: (A borrowed army kettle.) Coffee. Not as good. Don't tell them.

palace.text: They have a coffee machine in the officers' tent. Don't tell anyone I said it's better.
